pages.title: A Green Plan for Europe
pages.content:
The European Commission is part of the European Union (EU). On 11 December 2019, it shared a new plan. The name of the plan is the Green Deal. The Green Deal wants to protect our world. It wants a clean economy. By 2050, the EU wants its net greenhouse gas emissions to be zero. The plan wants to make work, factories, and everyday life more eco-friendly. This can help the climate and keep the world healthy.

One big goal is to use less and throw away less. The Green Deal helps a circular economy. In a circular economy, people repair, reuse, and recycle things. They do not throw them away. This protects nature. The Green Deal has many useful rules for this big change.

vocabulary.definition: Keep something safe.
The money, work, and business of a country.
A gas that keeps heat in the air and makes the Earth warmer.
Gases that cars and factories send into the air.
Good for nature, or not bad for it.
An economy in which people repair, reuse, and recycle things.
Use old things again to make new things.
Something that tells people what they must or must not do.

hotspots.title: Shared in 2019
hotspots.description: The European Commission shared the Green Deal on 11 December 2019.

hotspots.title: Repair and Reuse

exercises.title: Zero by 2050
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: What does the EU want by 2050?
options: net greenhouse gas emissions of zero
a new name for the plan
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says: “By 2050, the EU wants its net greenhouse gas emissions to be zero.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Zero net emissions is the big aim of the plan.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 1 again. Find “By 2050”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Wants to + Verb
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 1. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “The Green Deal wants to protect our world.” What comes after “wants to”?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “want to” we use the base verb: wants to protect, wants to make. The same form is in Chapter 1: “The plan wants to make work, factories, and everyday life more eco-friendly.”

feedback.correct: Good. Wants to + protect: the plan’s aim.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the word right after “wants to”. Is it an action?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Repair, Reuse, Recycle
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do people do in a circular economy?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: In a circular economy, people [blank], reuse, and [blank] things. They do not throw them [blank].
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “In a circular economy, people repair, reuse, and recycle things. They do not throw them away.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Repair, reuse, recycle: not throw away.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1. Find the three verbs together.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: My Green Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner three sentences about a green plan for your home.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do you want to do for a cleaner world?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “I want to use less water. I want to repair my old bag. I want to recycle paper at school.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: three different actions, each with “want to”.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Use less: “I want to use less …”
discussionPrompts.example: I want to use less water.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Repair: “I want to repair my …”
discussionPrompts.example: I want to repair my old bag.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Recycle: “I want to recycle …”
discussionPrompts.example: I want to recycle paper at school.

beforeYouRead.quote: On 11 December 2019, it shared a new plan.

pages.title: The Most Important Goals
pages.content:
Here are the most important goals of the Green Deal:

Fighting Climate Change: Climate change is a very important problem for the EU. By 2030, the EU and its countries want to make their greenhouse gas emissions at least 55% lower. By 2050, they want climate neutrality. This can slow down global warming and the problems that it brings.

Protecting Nature: The Green Deal wants people to use water, fields, and forests carefully. People must not cut down too many trees. We must not use too much water. Plants and animals must stay safe. The Green Deal also wants to repair nature. The goal is clean air, clean water, healthy fields, and healthy food for everyone.

A New Economy: The Green Deal helps green technology and eco-friendly businesses. In this way, the economy can grow, and nature can stay safe.

vocabulary.definition: Try hard to stop something bad.
When a country does not put more greenhouse gases into the air than it takes out.
The Earth slowly gets hotter.

hotspots.title: 55% Lower
hotspots.description: By 2030, the EU wants its greenhouse gas emissions to be at least 55% lower.

hotspots.title: Healthy Food for Everyone
hotspots.description: The goal is clean air, clean water, healthy fields, and healthy food for everyone.

exercises.title: Three Goals
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 2.
exercises.question: Which is NOT one of the three goals in Chapter 2?
exercises.explanation: The three goals are Fighting Climate Change, Protecting Nature, and A New Economy.

feedback.correct: Yes. Roads are not one of the three goals.
feedback.incorrect: Find the three titles with “:” in Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Must Not
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 2. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “People must not cut down too many trees.” What does “must not” mean here?
options: It is a good idea, but you can choose.
Do not do it. It is not OK.
You did it in the past.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Must not” (mustn’t) tells people that something is not OK. Chapter 2 also says: “We must not use too much water.”

feedback.correct: Good. Must not = do not do it.
feedback.incorrect: Think of a school rule: “You must not run in the corridor.” Can you choose to run?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Must or Must Not?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the right word for each sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits the goal?

formChoices.sentence: People [choice] cut down too many trees.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “People must not cut down too many trees. We must not use too much water. Plants and animals must stay safe.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Must for what we need, must not for what we stop.
feedback.incorrect: Read the Protecting Nature part of Chapter 2 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Green Class Rules
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write three green rules for your classroom with your partner.
languageFocusExercises.question: What must we do, and what must we not do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “We must turn off the lights. We must not throw paper on the floor. We must use both sides of the paper.”

feedback.correct: Check your rules: use “must” and “must not”.

discussionPrompts.question: Rule 1 — Do it: “We must …”
discussionPrompts.example: We must turn off the lights.

discussionPrompts.question: Rule 2 — Do not do it: “We must not …”
discussionPrompts.example: We must not throw paper on the floor.

discussionPrompts.question: Rule 3 — Your idea: “We must / must not …”
discussionPrompts.example: We must use both sides of the paper.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: By 2030, how much lower does the EU want its emissions?

iCan: I can name the three goals of the Green Deal.
I can use “must” and “must not” for rules.
I can say what the EU wants by 2030 and 2050.

pages.title: Why Is the Green Deal Important?
pages.content:
Climate change and pollution are a big danger for our world. Old ways of doing business use too much oil, coal, and gas. These are fossil fuels. We cannot use them like this for a long time. Many people think that a net-zero economy is the best way to fight climate change. It can also protect plants and animals and give us safe energy in the future.

Today, safe energy is a big problem. Because of wars and problems between countries, nobody knows what will happen next. Energy prices are high, and some goods cannot arrive on time. This is hard for many companies, especially for factories that use a lot of energy. Electricity, oil, and gas become expensive.

vocabulary.definition: Dirty air, water, or land.
A black stone that people burn to make heat.
Oil, coal, and gas from under the ground.
When the greenhouse gases that we put into the air are equal to the gases that we take out of it.

hotspots.title: Fossil Fuels
hotspots.description: Oil, coal, and gas are fossil fuels.

hotspots.title: Expensive Energy
hotspots.description: Because of wars and problems between countries, energy prices are high.

exercises.title: Why Is Energy a Problem?
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 3.
exercises.question: Why is safe energy a big problem today?
options: because of wars and problems between countries
because people use too little energy
because there are too many factories in the sea
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3 says: “Because of wars and problems between countries, nobody knows what will happen next.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Wars make energy prices high.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3. Find “Because of”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Too Much
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 3. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Old ways of doing business use too much oil, coal, and gas.” What does “too much” say?
options: They use more than is good.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Too much” means more than is good. We use it with things we cannot count: too much oil, too much water (Chapter 2).

feedback.correct: Good. Too much = more than is good.
feedback.incorrect: Is the sentence happy about the oil, coal, and gas? Read the next sentence: “We cannot use them like this for a long time.”

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Because Of, So
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happens, and why?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank] wars and problems between countries, nobody knows what will happen next. Energy prices are high, [blank] it is hard for many companies. Electricity, oil, and gas become [blank].
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Because of” + a noun gives the reason (because of wars). “So” gives the result (so it is hard for companies).

feedback.correct: Correct. Because of for the reason, so for the result.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3 again. Find the reason first, then the result.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Too Much at Home
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner about energy and water at home.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where do people use too much?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “Some people use too much water in the shower. Some people use too much electricity because of old lamps. So the bills are high.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: too much, because of, so.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Too much: “Some people use too much …”
discussionPrompts.example: Some people use too much water in the shower.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Why: “… because of …”
discussionPrompts.example: Some people use too much electricity because of old lamps.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Result: “So …”
discussionPrompts.example: So the bills are high.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
beforeYouRead.quote: Old ways of doing business use too much oil, coal, and gas.

iCan: I can say why fossil fuels are a problem.
I can use “too much”, “because of”, and “so”.
I can talk about energy at home.

pages.title: Energy from the Wind and the Sun
pages.content:
So, more and more countries are using renewable energy, like energy from the wind and the sun. It is often cheaper. With it, countries do not need expensive fossil fuels. To keep their factories strong, countries need new rules, more renewable energy, and workers with new skills.

So, the green change must be faster. Then factories can get clean energy at a good price. Countries and companies should make a big plan. The plan should show how much money new clean technology and new factories need.

vocabulary.definition: Energy from the wind and the sun, which never ends.
Something that you can do well because you learned it.

hotspots.title: Wind and Sun
hotspots.description: More and more countries are using energy from the wind and the sun.

hotspots.title: A Big Plan
hotspots.description: The plan should show how much money new clean technology and new factories need.

exercises.title: What Do Countries Need?
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 4.
exercises.question: To keep their factories strong, what do countries need?
options: new rules, more renewable energy, and workers with new skills
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says: “To keep their factories strong, countries need new rules, more renewable energy, and workers with new skills.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Rules, renewable energy, and new skills.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of the first paragraph of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Cheaper, Faster
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentences from Chapter 4. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “It is often cheaper.” “The green change must be faster.” What does -er do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Short adjectives take -er to compare: cheap → cheaper, fast → faster. Energy from the wind and the sun is cheaper than fossil fuels.

feedback.correct: Good. -er compares: cheaper than, faster than.
feedback.incorrect: Think: cheap → cheaper. Is it about one thing, or about two things side by side?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Compare Energy
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: How is renewable energy different?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Energy from the wind and the sun is often [blank] than oil and gas. The green change must be [blank]. Then factories can get [blank] energy at a good price.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “It is often cheaper.” “So, the green change must be faster. Then factories can get clean energy at a good price.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Cheaper, faster, clean.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 4 again. Which words are good news for factories?

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Compare Two Ways
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Compare two ways to go to school with your partner.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which way is better for the world?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “A bike is cheaper than a car. A bus is greener than a car. A car is faster, but it uses more fuel.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: -er + than.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Price: “A … is cheaper than a …”
discussionPrompts.example: A bike is cheaper than a car.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Nature: “A … is greener than a …”
discussionPrompts.example: A bus is greener than a car.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Your choice: “A … is faster, but …”
discussionPrompts.example: A car is faster, but it uses more fuel.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Is energy from the wind and the sun often cheaper or more expensive?

iCan: I can say why countries use wind and sun energy.
I can compare with -er: cheaper, faster.
I can compare two ways to travel.

pages.title: New Opportunities
pages.content:
In the next 20 or 30 years, a net-zero time may start. At that time, the gases that we put into the air will be the same as the gases that we take out. This new economy will bring new markets, new clean technology, and new ways to make energy. Some countries spend money on clean technology early and move fast. These countries can have a strong place in the new economy. They can also be the best in the world at clean technology and at fighting climate change.

The green economy brings new kinds of factories and jobs. These jobs need workers with new skills. Factories also become modern and eco-friendly. To help, the EU made a law. Its name is the Net-Zero Industry Act. It helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels. It also helps Europe build machines that catch carbon dioxide and keep it in a safe place.

vocabulary.definition: An official rule of a country.
A tall machine that makes electricity from the wind.
A machine that makes a building warm or cool.
A flat object that makes electricity from the sun.
A gas that comes from burning oil, coal, and gas.

hotspots.title: The Net-Zero Industry Act
hotspots.description: The EU made a law. Its name is the Net-Zero Industry Act.

hotspots.title: Green Machines
hotspots.description: It helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels.

exercises.title: A New Law
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 5.
exercises.question: What does the Net-Zero Industry Act help Europe build?
options: batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5 says: “It helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels.”

feedback.correct: Yes. These are green technologies.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5. Find the name of the law.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Will and May
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentences from Chapter 5. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “A net-zero time may start.” “This new economy will bring new markets.” Which word is less sure?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Will” says we are sure about the future. “May” says it is possible, but we are not sure. Chapter 5 is sure about new markets, but not sure about the exact time.

feedback.correct: Good. May = possible; will = sure.
feedback.incorrect: Read the two sentences again. Which one sounds like a guess?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: The Net-Zero Future
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What will the new economy bring?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: In the next 20 or 30 years, a net-zero time [blank] start. This new economy [blank] bring new markets, new clean technology, and new ways to make [blank].
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “a net-zero time may start … This new economy will bring new markets, new clean technology, and new ways to make energy.”

feedback.correct: Correct. May for possible, will for sure.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 5. Look for the future words.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: My Town in 2050
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner about your town in 2050.
languageFocusExercises.question: What will your town be like in 2050?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “In 2050, there will be solar panels on many roofs. Buses will use electricity. There may be a wind turbine on the hill.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: will for sure, may for possible.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Sure: “In 2050, there will be …”
discussionPrompts.example: In 2050, there will be solar panels on many roofs.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Sure: “… will …”
discussionPrompts.example: Buses will use electricity.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Possible: “There may be …”
discussionPrompts.example: There may be a wind turbine on the hill.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: When may a net-zero time start?
beforeYouRead.quote: In the next 20 or 30 years, a net-zero time may start.

iCan: I can name green technologies from the story.
I can use “will” and “may” for the future.
I can talk about my town in 2050.

pages.title: New Rules for Green Things
pages.content: New rules for eco-friendly things are important too. They help people build, reuse, and recycle green technology. For example, big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought. Other rules make spare parts easy to find, so people can repair their things. In the future, these rules will be for many more everyday things. Factories will have to follow these rules and protect nature.

vocabulary.definition: A new part for a machine when an old part is broken.

hotspots.title: No Throwing Away
hotspots.description: Big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought.

hotspots.title: Spare Parts
hotspots.description: Other rules make spare parts easy to find, so people can repair their things.

exercises.title: Why Spare Parts?
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 6.
exercises.question: Why do the rules make spare parts easy to find?
options: so people can repair their things
so shops can sell more new things
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “Other rules make spare parts easy to find, so people can repair their things.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Repair is better than throwing away.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 6 again. Find “so people can”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Cannot for Rules
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 6. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought.” What does “cannot” say here?
options: They are not able to lift the clothes.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Can” and “cannot” often talk about rules: what people are allowed or not allowed to do. Chapter 6 also says factories “will have to follow these rules”.

feedback.correct: Good. Here cannot = a rule says no.
feedback.incorrect: Is this about strength, or about a rule? Read the first sentence of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: So People Can
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do the new rules do?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: New rules help people build, reuse, and [blank] green technology. Other rules make spare parts easy to [blank], so people can [blank] their things.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “They help people build, reuse, and recycle green technology … Other rules make spare parts easy to find, so people can repair their things.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Recycle, find, repair.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 6 again. Which words are good for nature?

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Something I Repaired
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner about a thing you can repair.
languageFocusExercises.question: What can you repair at home?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “My bike is old, but I can repair it. I need a new spare part for the brake. So I can use my bike again.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: can, a spare part, so.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — The thing: “My … is old, but I can repair it.”
discussionPrompts.example: My bike is old, but I can repair it.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — What you need: “I need a …”
discussionPrompts.example: I need a new spare part for the brake.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Result: “So I can …”
discussionPrompts.example: So I can use my bike again.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What can big companies in the EU NOT throw away?
beforeYouRead.quote: big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought

iCan: I can explain two new EU rules.
I can use “can” and “cannot” for rules.
I can talk about repairing my things.

pages.title: Smart Shopping and Green Jobs
pages.content:
In fact, the Green Deal needs people to buy smart, eco-friendly things. For this, people need clear information. Before they buy something, they should see how green and strong it is. Then they can choose green things. For example, fridges and washing machines have energy labels. With these labels, people can easily see which one is better. More information helps the green change.

The green change is also changing jobs. In the last few years, the number of green jobs has grown fast. Workers need new skills, so countries need big training programs. Clean energy companies and eco-friendly factories need more workers. In the future, companies will try hard to find workers with the right skills.

vocabulary.definition: A label that shows how much energy a machine uses.

hotspots.title: Energy Labels
hotspots.description: Fridges and washing machines have energy labels.

hotspots.title: Green Jobs
hotspots.description: In the last few years, the number of green jobs has grown fast.

exercises.title: Before You Buy
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: What do people need before they buy something?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7 says: “For this, people need clear information.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Clear information helps people choose green things.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 7.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Should
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 7. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Before they buy something, they should see how green and strong it is.” What does “should” give?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Should” gives advice. It says what is a good idea. After “should” we use the base verb: should see, should check.

feedback.correct: Good. Should = a good idea.
feedback.incorrect: Is the sentence telling a story, or giving a good idea to shoppers?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Jobs Are Changing
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: How are jobs changing?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: In the last few years, the number of green jobs has [blank] fast. Workers need new [blank], so countries need big [blank] programs.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “In the last few years, the number of green jobs has grown fast. Workers need new skills, so countries need big training programs.” Has grown = it started in the past and is true now.

feedback.correct: Correct. Has grown, skills, training.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 7. Look after “has”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Advice for a Shopper
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Give a friend advice before they buy a new fridge.
languageFocusExercises.question: What should your friend do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “You should look at the energy label. You should choose a strong fridge. You should not buy a big fridge for one person.”

feedback.correct: Check your advice: should and should not + a verb.

discussionPrompts.question: Advice 1 — The label: “You should look at …”
discussionPrompts.example: You should look at the energy label.

discussionPrompts.question: Advice 2 — Strong: “You should choose …”
discussionPrompts.example: You should choose a strong fridge.

discussionPrompts.question: Advice 3 — Do not: “You should not …”
discussionPrompts.example: You should not buy a big fridge for one person.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Where can you see an energy label?
beforeYouRead.quote: fridges and washing machines have energy labels

iCan: I can say what an energy label shows.
I can give advice with “should”.
I can say how jobs are changing.

pages.title: Learning and Working Together
pages.content:
Finally, the green change needs good education. Countries must train workers and teach people well. This is important for strong factories, for a fair change for everyone, and for net-zero goals. So, education is a big part of the Green Deal. It helps everyone learn green and digital skills. Education and training are important for the future of our world.

Countries, companies, and people should all help with these plans. Then these ideas can become real actions for a cleaner world. Climate change is a problem for every country in the world. So, it is good for countries to work together with their partners. Türkiye also made its own Green Deal Action Plan in 2021. Its goal is net-zero emissions by 2053.

vocabulary.definition: Teaching and learning, for example at school.

hotspots.title: Learning for the Future
hotspots.description: Education helps everyone learn green and digital skills.

hotspots.title: Türkiye’s Plan
hotspots.description: Türkiye made its own Green Deal Action Plan in 2021. Its goal is net-zero emissions by 2053.

exercises.title: Türkiye’s Goal
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 8.
exercises.question: What is the goal of Türkiye’s Green Deal Action Plan?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 says: “Its goal is net-zero emissions by 2053.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Türkiye’s goal is net zero by 2053.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last two sentences of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: It Is Good for … to …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 8. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “It is good for countries to work together with their partners.” Who should work together?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “It is good for + people + to + verb” says that an action is a good idea for those people. The same idea is in Chapter 8: “Education and training are important for the future of our world.”

feedback.correct: Good. It is good for countries to work together.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the word after “for”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Learning Together
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Why is education a big part of the Green Deal?

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Chapter 8: “Countries must train workers and teach people well … It helps everyone learn green and digital skills … Climate change is a problem for every country in the world.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Train, digital, country.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 8 again. Find “must”, “skills”, and “every”.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Students: “It is good for students to learn …”
discussionPrompts.example: It is good for students to learn about solar panels.

pages.title: Key Facts
pages.content: One fact from every chapter. Each chapter stamp colors its stop.

facts.label: 11 December
facts.title: The European Commission shares the Green Deal.
facts.text: By 2050, the EU wants its net greenhouse gas emissions to be zero.

facts.label: By
facts.title: At least 55% lower greenhouse gas emissions.
facts.text: By 2050, the EU wants climate neutrality.

facts.label: Today
facts.title: Safe energy is a big problem.
facts.text: Because of wars and problems between countries, electricity, oil, and gas become expensive.

facts.label: Now
facts.title: More and more countries are using renewable energy.
facts.text: It is often cheaper than fossil fuels.

facts.label: In 20 or 30 years
facts.title: A net-zero time may start.
facts.text: The Net-Zero Industry Act helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels.

facts.label: New
facts.title: Big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought.
facts.text: Spare parts must be easy to find, so people can repair their things.

facts.label: In the shops
facts.title: Energy labels help people compare fridges and washing machines.
facts.text: The number of green jobs has grown fast.

facts.label: Türkiye
facts.title: Türkiye makes its own Green Deal Action Plan.
facts.text: Its goal is net-zero emissions by 2053.

pages.title: Knowledge Check
pages.content: Test your understanding of the A2 text about the European Green Deal.

exercises.title: Who Shared It?
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Who shared the Green Deal on 11 December 2019?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “The European Commission is part of the European Union (EU). On 11 December 2019, it shared a new plan.”

feedback.correct: Yes. The European Commission is part of the EU.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first two sentences of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: The 2030 Goal
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: By 2030, the EU wants its greenhouse gas emissions to be at least 55% lower.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “By 2030, the EU and its countries want to make their greenhouse gas emissions at least 55% lower.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is true.
feedback.incorrect: Read the Fighting Climate Change part of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Fossil Fuels
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Which three are fossil fuels?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “Old ways of doing business use too much oil, coal, and gas. These are fossil fuels.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Oil, coal, and gas come from under the ground.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Wind and Sun
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Energy from the wind and the sun is often more expensive than fossil fuels.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “It is often cheaper. With it, countries do not need expensive fossil fuels.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false. It is often cheaper.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4 again.

exercises.title: The Law
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: What is the name of the EU law in Chapter 5?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “To help, the EU made a law. Its name is the Net-Zero Industry Act.”

feedback.correct: Yes. It helps Europe build green technologies.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Clothes Nobody Bought
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “For example, big companies in the EU cannot throw away clothes that nobody bought.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is true.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: Energy Labels
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: What do energy labels help people do?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “With these labels, people can easily see which one is better.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Labels help shoppers choose.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: Türkiye
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: When does Türkiye want to reach net-zero emissions?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8: “Its goal is net-zero emissions by 2053.”

feedback.correct: Yes. 2053 is Türkiye’s goal.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 8.

pages.title: Master Glossary
pages.content: Review all key vocabulary from the text in one place.

vocabulary.definition: Keep something safe.
vocabulary.storyExample: The Green Deal wants to protect our world.

vocabulary.definition: The money, work, and business of a country.
vocabulary.storyExample: It wants a clean economy.

vocabulary.definition: A gas that keeps heat in the air and makes the Earth warmer.
vocabulary.storyExample: By 2050, the EU wants its net greenhouse gas emissions to be zero.

vocabulary.definition: Gases that cars and factories send into the air.
vocabulary.storyExample: By 2050, the EU wants its net greenhouse gas emissions to be zero.

vocabulary.definition: Good for nature, or not bad for it.
vocabulary.storyExample: The plan wants to make work, factories, and everyday life more eco-friendly.

vocabulary.definition: An economy in which people repair, reuse, and recycle things.
vocabulary.storyExample: The Green Deal helps a circular economy.

vocabulary.definition: Use old things again to make new things.
vocabulary.storyExample: In a circular economy, people repair, reuse, and recycle things.

vocabulary.definition: Something that tells people what they must or must not do.
vocabulary.storyExample: The Green Deal has many useful rules for this big change.

vocabulary.definition: Try hard to stop something bad.
vocabulary.storyExample: Here are the most important goals of the Green Deal: Fighting Climate Change: Climate change is a very important problem for the EU.

vocabulary.definition: When a country does not put more greenhouse gases into the air than it takes out.
vocabulary.storyExample: By 2050, they want climate neutrality.

vocabulary.definition: The Earth slowly gets hotter.
vocabulary.storyExample: This can slow down global warming and the problems that it brings.

vocabulary.definition: Dirty air, water, or land.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: Why Is the Green Deal Important?
vocabulary.storyExample: Climate change and pollution are a big danger for our world.

vocabulary.definition: A black stone that people burn to make heat.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: Why Is the Green Deal Important?
vocabulary.storyExample: Old ways of doing business use too much oil, coal, and gas.

vocabulary.definition: Oil, coal, and gas from under the ground.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: Why Is the Green Deal Important?
vocabulary.storyExample: These are fossil fuels.

vocabulary.definition: When the greenhouse gases that we put into the air are equal to the gases that we take out of it.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: Why Is the Green Deal Important?
vocabulary.storyExample: Many people think that a net-zero economy is the best way to fight climate change.

vocabulary.definition: Energy from the wind and the sun, which never ends.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: Energy from the Wind and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: So, more and more countries are using renewable energy, like energy from the wind and the sun.

vocabulary.definition: Something that you can do well because you learned it.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: Energy from the Wind and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: To keep their factories strong, countries need new rules, more renewable energy, and workers with new skills.

vocabulary.definition: An official rule of a country.
vocabulary.storyExample: To help, the EU made a law.

vocabulary.definition: A tall machine that makes electricity from the wind.
vocabulary.storyExample: It helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels.

vocabulary.definition: A machine that makes a building warm or cool.
vocabulary.storyExample: It helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels.

vocabulary.definition: A flat object that makes electricity from the sun.
vocabulary.storyExample: It helps Europe build batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, and solar panels.

vocabulary.definition: A gas that comes from burning oil, coal, and gas.
vocabulary.storyExample: It also helps Europe build machines that catch carbon dioxide and keep it in a safe place.

vocabulary.definition: A new part for a machine when an old part is broken.
vocabulary.storyExample: Other rules make spare parts easy to find, so people can repair their things.

vocabulary.definition: A label that shows how much energy a machine uses.
vocabulary.storyExample: For example, fridges and washing machines have energy labels.

vocabulary.definition: Teaching and learning, for example at school.
vocabulary.storyExample: Finally, the green change needs good education.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the language from all eight chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Must, Must Not
exercises.instructions: Put each sentence in the right group.
exercises.question: Is it something we need to do, or something we must stop?

dragDropGroups.group: Must: we need to do it
items: Plants and animals must stay safe.
Countries must train workers and teach people well.
So, the green change must be faster.
People must not cut down too many trees.
We must not use too much water.

Must: we need to do it: Plants and animals must stay safe.
Countries must train workers and teach people well.
So, the green change must be faster.
Must not: stop it: People must not cut down too many trees.
We must not use too much water.

exercises.explanation: “Must” says something is necessary (Chapters 2, 4, 8). “Must not” says it is not OK (Chapter 2).

feedback.correct: Correct. Must for what is needed, must not for what we stop.
feedback.incorrect: Read each sentence. Is there “not” after “must”?

exercises.title: Practise: Compare
exercises.instructions: Choose the right form for each sentence.
exercises.question: Which form compares two things?

formChoices.sentence: Energy from the wind and the sun is often [choice] than fossil fuels.
By 2030, the EU wants emissions at least 55% [choice].

exercises.explanation: Chapters 2 and 4 compare with -er: lower, cheaper, faster.

feedback.correct: Correct. -er compares.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a comparison: than, or a change from now.

exercises.title: Practise: Will, May, Should
exercises.instructions: Choose the right word for each sentence from the text.
exercises.question: Sure, possible, or a good idea?

formChoices.sentence: This new economy [choice] bring new markets.
In the next 20 or 30 years, a net-zero time [choice] start.
Before they buy something, they [choice] see how green and strong it is.

exercises.explanation: Will = sure (Chapter 5). May = possible (Chapter 5). Should = a good idea (Chapter 7).

feedback.correct: Correct. Will, may, should.
feedback.incorrect: Think: is it sure, possible, or advice?

exercises.title: Use: A Green Week
exercises.instructions: Plan a green week for your class with the book’s language.
exercises.question: What will your class do?
exercises.explanation: Example: “We want to recycle paper. We must not waste water. A bike is cheaper than a car. We will repair one old thing. We should look at energy labels.”

feedback.correct: Check your plan: want to, must not, -er, will, should.

discussionPrompts.question: Monday — Want to: “We want to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We want to recycle paper.

discussionPrompts.question: Tuesday — A rule: “We must not …”
discussionPrompts.example: We must not waste water.

discussionPrompts.question: Wednesday — Compare: “A … is cheaper than a …”
discussionPrompts.example: A bike is cheaper than a car.

discussionPrompts.question: Thursday — Future: “We will repair …”
discussionPrompts.example: We will repair one old thing.

discussionPrompts.question: Friday — Advice: “We should …”
discussionPrompts.example: We should look at energy labels.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Show what you understand from the whole text about the European Green Deal.

exercises.title: The Big Aim
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer.
exercises.question: What is the main aim of the Green Deal?
options: to make the EU’s net greenhouse gas emissions zero by 2050
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “By 2050, the EU wants its net greenhouse gas emissions to be zero.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Net zero by 2050.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Circular Economy
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: In a circular economy, people throw things away quickly.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “In a circular economy, people repair, reuse, and recycle things. They do not throw them away.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Protecting Nature
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer.
exercises.question: What is the goal of Protecting Nature?
options: clean air, clean water, healthy fields, and healthy food for everyone
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “The goal is clean air, clean water, healthy fields, and healthy food for everyone.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Clean and healthy for everyone.
feedback.incorrect: Read the Protecting Nature part of Chapter 2.

shows how much energy a machine uses

exercises.title: Green Jobs
exercises.instructions: Choose the best answer.
exercises.question: Why do countries need big training programs?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “Workers need new skills, so countries need big training programs.”

feedback.correct: Yes. New jobs need new skills.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: Working Together

exercises.question: The text says climate change is a problem only for Europe.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8: “Climate change is a problem for every country in the world.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false. It is a problem for every country.

exercises.instructions: Put the events in time order.

sequencingItems.text: The European Commission shares the Green Deal (2019).
Türkiye makes its Green Deal Action Plan (2021).
The EU wants at least 55% lower emissions (2030).

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the years of the Green Deal.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the years in brackets and put them from small to big.

exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about your own green step.

exercises.explanation: Example: “I want to use less electricity. I will repair my old things. It is good for my family to recycle.”
